original_test_intent: Verify the Socket Designation string of every SMBIOS Type 7 cache record matches the approved cache-instance naming scheme and remains attached to the same cache handle, level and Type 4 relationship after reboot; the string is not automatically a physical CPU socket identifier.
original_method: Capture complete raw/decoded Type 7 records, retain each designation string index/value with handle and decoded cache level/configuration, resolve inbound Type 4 L1/L2/L3 handles where present, compare with the approved cache naming/topology map, reboot and repeat.
manual_activity: A user approves the Type 7 designation naming scheme, its cache-level/topology meaning and reboot plan. Collection, relationship resolution and comparison are automatable.
required_inputs: Expected Socket Designation string per Type 7 handle/cache instance
Definition of whether names encode cache level, CPU socket, bank or vendor-specific instance
Expected inbound Type 4 cache-handle relationships and shared-cache policy
Validated Type 4/Type 7 parser plus approved reboot and OOB recovery plan
safety_requirements: Read SMBIOS only; do not alter cache, CPU, BIOS or firmware state.
Preserve raw string index, full Type 7 handle/configuration and decoded designation; grep fragments cannot bind repeated labels to cache identity.
Do not interpret the name as a physical CPU socket without an approved mapping; `Socket Designation` is a descriptive cache string.
Resolve Type 4 references separately so a stable label cannot hide a wrong or dangling cache relationship.
Stop on malformed string indices, duplicate/ambiguous naming beyond policy, relationship drift or reboot failure; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Collect complete Type 7 records, resolve designation strings and Type 4 references, compare naming and cache identity before/after reboot.
Do not rename metadata, infer undocumented physical-socket meaning or decide PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the Type 7 naming/topology map and allowed normalization/blank/shared-cache rules.
Approve reboot/recovery and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The field label is correct, but the grep suppresses errors and loses Type 7 handle, cache level/configuration and inbound Type 4 relationship context.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Archive complete Type 7 raw/decoded records and relevant Type 4 cache handles, retaining designation string index/value per handle and validating the approved naming/topology graph.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Type 7 Socket Designation scope, cache script and 5/5-minute values are retained.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Resolve each Type 7 designation string with raw index provenance, bind it to handle/cache configuration and validate the approved naming scheme plus Type 4 references before and after reboot.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record SMBIOS, BIOS, CPU/cache topology and parser/dmidecode versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Applicable SMBIOS Type 7 Socket Designation string semantics, Type 4 cache-handle semantics, approved platform cache topology and installed tool documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds cache identity, string-index provenance and relationship mapping while avoiding an unsupported physical-socket assumption.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; detects stable names attached to wrong cache records or relationships.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The designation is firmware-defined descriptive text and may not match OS cache IDs or physical silk-screen labels.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve vendor-specific names or aliases per cache handle/level, but must define them explicitly and may not use the string alone as proof of physical CPU-socket ownership.
expected_evidence: Approved Type 7 designation/cache map, semantics, normalization and tool versions
Complete pre-reboot Type 7 table with handle, raw string index/value, cache configuration/level and decoded designation
Relevant Type 4-to-Type 7 reference graph and naming consistency result
Approved reboot/health evidence and equivalent post-reboot comparison
Engineer verdict with any documented vendor naming convention
